title: A well-formed JSON array pasted as the request is shape-detected as a vendor feed, not a BidRequest
specNotes: OpenRTB 2.6 §3.2.1 defines BidRequest as an object, never an array — so a well-formed request never looks like this on the wire. `detectType()` (packages/core/detect.js) has no concept of which UI field a payload came from: `validate()` is one function called identically on whatever is pasted into either pane (core-run.js calls it the same way for both `values.request` and `values.response`), and any array root is routed to the vendor push-materials feed validator regardless of slot — every array-rooted vendor shape documented elsewhere in this corpus (push-x-richads-bare-array, pop-adon3-*, push-ppcmate-multi, …) is itself a RESPONSE, but nothing in the architecture enforces that at the type-detection layer.

This is recorded as the tool's actual, consistent, documented decision rule (core-validate map §4: 'Array root: VENDOR_FEED unconditionally'), not a spec violation to gap: the IAB specification has no opinion on which UI field a tool exposes for which payload, and shape-based (rather than slot-based) detection is this product's architecture end to end. The array item is deliberately well-formed by every push-material field rule so the case demonstrates the full extent of the behavior: a genuinely clean vendor-response payload is classified 'clean' when pasted as a request, with the type label ('Push-Materials Feed Response') being the only signal that it was not read as a BidRequest.

A person relying on the type label to notice the mismatch is a real but separate UI/UX question (does the Inspector's own chrome make the type label prominent enough on the request side); that question belongs to the UI/UX pass, not to a Core protocol-compliance gap.
